behavior: A dry run names every deployment of the project once, marks the one answering to `<project>.pages.dev` as kept, and issues no HTTP write
verification: uv run pytest tests/test_prune_deployments.py -q -k 'dry_run or token_travels'

behavior: `--apply` deletes every deployment but the keeper, one call each, and a failed delete stops the run non-zero with the deployments after it left alone
verification: uv run pytest tests/test_prune_deployments.py -q -k 'alias_holder or failed_delete'

behavior: When the project names no canonical deployment, or names one absent from the deployment list, the script refuses and deletes nothing, even with `--apply`
A deployment whose build has not settled is skipped rather than deleted, and pagination is followed so every page of the project is covered
verification: uv run pytest tests/test_prune_deployments.py -q -k 'building or pagination'

behavior: The token travels to curl on stdin and never on argv or in the output, and a run without `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` refuses before calling the API
verification: uv run pytest tests/test_prune_deployments.py -q -k 'token or credential'

behavior: `make prune-deployments` exists and the decommission runbook's step 4 names it, keeping the dashboard path as the fallback
verification: make -n prune-deployments >/dev/null && uv run pytest tests/test_decommission_runbook.py -q
